newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament hears how police killed reporter.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament hears how police killed reporter.

text.p: The Turkish parliament on Tuesday heard how police beat journalist Metin Goktepe to death in an Istanbul sports complex after taking him into custody.

"The reports of inspectors and the testimony of witnesses show that Goktepe was beaten while being taken to the sport centre, in the sport centre and in the downstairs of the centre," Hakan Tartan, head of a parliamentary commission investigating the murder, told his fellow MPs.
Goktepe, 27, was found dead on January 8, 1996, near a gymnasium complex after being detained by police while covering the funeral of two militant leftists.
The official autopsy report said Goktepe, a reporter for the leftist daily Evrensel, died from a brain haemorrhage brought on by blows to the head.

"I think Goktepe was hit in the confusion while being detained. If he had been taken to hospital he could have been saved," Tartan quoted Orhan Tasanlar, police chief of Istanbul at the time of the incident, as telling the commission.
The opened an inquiry into the death of Goktepe and submitted a report to parliament leaders in June.
Forty-eight police officers have been charged in connection with Goktepe's death. They face sentences of between three to seven years if convicted.
However, such convictions and even public discussion of alleged police brutality are rare in Turkey, despite repeated pledges by the political leadership to end abuses.
